messages:
Alex: Quick Q — seeing intermittent 503s because requests meant for payments-v2 land on legacy. Two routes look overlapping, can someone confirm the exact matcher precedence?

Alex: Route snippets:
```yaml
- match:
    host: "api.company.com"
    path: "/v1/payments"
  service: payments-v2

- match:
    host: "*.company.com"
    path_prefix: "/v1/"
    headers:
      - name: "X-Variant"
        value: "legacy"
  service: legacy
```

Maya: Host exact should be preferred over wildcard, and exact path over prefix. Headers are additional filters, not a higher-precedence dimension. But our current behavior seems fuzzy. :thinking_face: 

Sam: From runtime notes I remember: we compute a specificity score by host then path. Headers increment score but don't outrank a strictly more specific host+path. So exact host+exact path beats wildcard+prefix+headers.

Linh: We need to be explicit. Proposed rule (informal):
- Step 1: host specificity (exact > wildcard with fewer globs > catch-all)
- Step 2: path specificity (exact > regex > prefix > catch-all)
- Step 3: add header/method/query matches as bonuses (they narrow candidate set but should not let a less-specific host/path win)
- Tie-breaker: deterministic stable ID ordering (not creation time) so rollouts don't flip unexpectedly.

Maya: I think regex > prefix is important — people rely on regex to be able to capture and make decisions. But regexs are tricky because they can be both broader or narrower than prefix. We should score regex by pattern length/complexity heuristics.

Sam: Agreed. Runtime can score regex by measured specificity: e.g., number of literal chars + number of capturing groups penalties. That gives consistent ordering.

deploy-bot: lint 1815123456: ambiguous match detected between route[0] and route[1] for host candidates (api.company.com vs *.company.com). Recommend making first route explicitly prioritized or adding header match.

Alex: Ok, concrete ask: can we update the docs + lint rules to:
- document host/path/header precedence as above
- make lint warn when a wildcard host + prefix would shadow an exact path for a different host pattern
- console UX: tooltip that shows which rule won and why (score breakdown)

Linh: I'll take runtime + lint PRs. Plan:
1) implement scoring function (host score + path score + header bonus + regex heuristic)
2) update router-lint to emit actionable warning with examples
3) docs + console tooltip changes (small copy + scoring breakdown)
4) add unit tests that reproduce Alex's 503 case

Maya: Nice. One more edge: trailing slash normalization. We should make canonicalization explicit — exact match must match canonical form, prefix should ignore trailing slash differences. Add that to doc too. :memo:

Sam: Also confirm that method and query params are only used if present in the matcher and otherwise don't influence precedence. Document that.

Alex: Thanks all. Assigning to @Linh. Please @me when PRs are opened — I'll add the failing request trace to the test. :eyes:

Linh: Will do. Opening PRs today, ping when you have the trace.

Maya: Great, this should stop the flakey routing.

Sam: +1 to deterministic tie-breaker instead of creation time (avoids rollout-induced flips).

Alex: Cool — closing the loop here.
